The #BlackLivesMatter movement became an international phenomenon in 2020. As protesters took to the streets in cities across the U.S. in the aftermath of the police killing of George Floyd, so too did people in other countries. https://t.co/Uu79f6rsLD

Photos of this year's #BlackLivesMatter demonstrations depicted joy, love, and unity, rejecting the trope that protest images must convey only violent conflict. @mylmarche and Nicole Mo examine the legacy of movement photography in @TheAtlantic. https://t.co/IGxUaxtddn

On June 1, 2020, at the height of the #BlackLivesMatter protests last summer, DC police arrested more than five times as many people on unrest-related charges than they did during Wednesday’s insurrection at the U.S. Capitol. https://t.co/XSVHh5vspq
Today Trayvon Martin should be celebrating his 26th birthday. #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/UCiUnWjDRB

#OTD in 1968, S. Carolina Highway Patrol officers killed 3 Black students and injured 28 others in what came to be known as the Orangeburg Massacre. The students had been protesting to desegregate a local bowling alley. #BlackHistoryMonth #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/HHNKqneq1V

Ahmaud Arbery should be here today. He should've been able to vote in the election. He should've seen his 26th birthday. His tragic killing stands as a reminder of why we can never allow white supremacy to go unchecked. #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/B8Xgxzz9qH

Today marks 9 years since the tragic murder of Trayvon Martin, who was fatally shot as he walked home from buying candy at a store. Trayvon was a victim of racial discrimination and inequality. He deserves justice. He was only 17. #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/L7XzcRotna

Tarika Wilson was an innocent bystander. She was hiding with her children & shielding her baby when a Lima Police Officer fired shots at her bedroom killing her & striking her one-year-old child. The officer was acquitted of all charges. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/pduwpksBch

Eleanor Bumpurs' story highlights many of the same challenges we face today. Eleanor deserved to be met by trained professionals who could treat her with care and empathy. Instead, her life was stolen from her. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/gZm4J6WFZO

A call for assistance should never be a death sentence. Tanisha Anderson was experiencing a mental health crisis when a knee was put to her back by Cleveland Police. Both officers involved were cleared of criminal wrongdoing. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/XiEY9VYKaJ

Black trans women are the most marginalized in every way and disproportionately vulnerable to violence.  Black trans women must be protected, and the culture of violence that makes them most vulnerable must be dismantled. Kayla's story matters. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/bs2I1FNlDU

Aiyana was a child with a full life ahead of her. Police were raiding the wrong home when she was killed. She’ll never get to graduate college. She’ll never get to vote. The officer responsible for her death was never held responsible. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/3llApMY3f6

For Black people, the threat of police violence looms over every movement in public spaces. Officer Servin opened fire on the group, falsely claiming one of Rekia’s friends approached him with a gun. It was a cell phone. Rekia had done nothing wrong. #SayHerName #BlackLivesMatter https://t.co/oyFqH4j1FC
